12-crud-api.note: Full six-case typed HTTP CRUD contract plus generated flows proven in actual compiled H-Code, independent JS interpreter and frozen TypeScript correctness oracle; NOT a competitive idiomatic TypeScript baseline.

13-form-validation-ui.originalAcceptance: interactive required/email validation with accessible error feedback
13-form-validation-ui.note: Native Rust/browser ESM, independent H-Code JS interpreter, and actual Chromium against independent idiomatic TS; one task only. Source and browser input fixtures SHA-locked.

14-todo-app.note: All task14 business behavior is source-authored H-Code, independent JS and TypeScript app. Real Chrome executes 15 steps over 3 separate browser launches for each engine and checks durable JSON plus accessible list and live status. Per-task source savings are below the 70% goal.

15-db-dashboard.note: Real Chromium, independent Rust ESM/H-Code JS interpreter/idiomatic TS, five SQL-free SQLite fixtures, Unicode ties and source hashes. HTTP server validates ISO dates before execution. Does not imply all 20 tasks pass.

16-auth-sessions.acceptance: issue/rotate/revoke a signed session using deterministic fixture identity
16-auth-sessions.limitations: Only task16: symmetric HMAC-authenticated stateful session for one fixed fixture identity. No expiration, production credential provider, JWT or asymmetric signature claim. JS language evaluator is independent but shares the generic HTTP/CAS host with native; TypeScript uses independent SQLite transactions. Whole app source includes validation, configuration and persistence glue. JSON fixtures are separate and inclusive; generated runtime is separate, and Node/Rust/toolchain/SQLite size is not zero or measured here. No global median, runtime-performance or AI-token claim.

17-websocket-chat.acceptance: two isolated clients, room join, ordered message delivery and disconnect
17-websocket-chat.limitations: Only task17. Independent language evaluator shares the generic transport with native; TypeScript owns separate application/routing logic but both use maintained ws. Primary clients use Node standard WebSocket; forced-disconnect clients run in separate killed processes. Counter-boundary runs use temporary initialization variants. No authentication, TLS, persistence, offline delivery or multi-process room claim. Complete app source includes configuration, protocol/input and transport glue. Shared JSON, dependency/metadata and emitted runtime are separate. No global median, runtime-performance or AI-token claim.

18-refactor-task.acceptance: refactor a frozen baseline without modifying its required behavior or assertions
18-refactor-task.limitations: Only task18. All project modules, types, fixture readers and tests count as authored source. Shared JSON input is separate and included in alternate totals. Generated JS includes duplicated runtime per test file. No speed, AI-token, toolchain-size or global median claim. The JS reference has no local module loader and is not counted.

19-bug-repair-task.acceptance: reproduce seeded failure, fix actual root cause and verify regression test
19-bug-repair-task.limitations: Only task19. Seed and repair are benchmark fixtures, not a production incident or timing study. All modules, old/new tests, types and fixture readers count. Both shared JSON files have separate and inclusive totals. Generated runtime is separate and depends on resolved paths. The JS reference has no local module loader. No global median, performance or AI-token claim.

20-incremental-feature.acceptance: extend frozen starter app while retaining all prior behavior and passing new acceptance
20-incremental-feature.limitations: Only task20. Starter CLI is established and committed before extension, derived from task18 modules. Whole extended project counts, including old/new tests, both CLI entries, input readers and types. Shared data and CLI outcomes are separate and inclusive; generated runtime is separate. Independent JS reference has no local module loader. No global median, universal floating-point, runtime-performance or AI-token claim.

explanation: Full verification derives from source-locked compiler executions and independent comparisons. Task18 requires unchanged frozen tests on actual before/after Rust-compiled and TypeScript projects; it does not claim a local-module JS reference engine. Original preregistration remains SHA-frozen and unsupported tasks stay in the denominator. Correctness oracles are not automatically competitive TypeScript baselines. No global twenty-workload 70% median has been computed.
